key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation relative to BA spacers under ambient light and thermal stress.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but practical devices also require structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or device-level efficiency tests, so improved material durability should not be equated with proven solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
